subject: interpreting fit measures from runMI on imputed data

messages.author: cf1bcefdbd38a662
messages.subject: interpreting fit measures from runMI on imputed data
parts:
Sunthud and Alex helped me to get runMI working on my imputed dataset (details here). I'm able to fit the model on the imputed data, but something is not quite right, and I'm pretty sure the problem is conceptual. 

I've trimmed the model and data to just 4 variables. I want to look at the fit for a one factor model I'm calling total. I was using the WLSMV estimator on ordered factors, but I converted the data to numeric to make the examples more straightforward.

In the first example I use runMI on the imputed data. In the second example I just run a normal cfa on 1 of the 20 imputed datasets. I thought the problem might be with runMI, but I get the same type of fit statistics when running lavaan directly on 1 dataset.

Do the fit indices suggest a data problem? Or is something else going on?

library(lavaan)
library(semTools) # see linked thread about updating to 04-11
library(devtools)

# read in data from gist (list of 20 dataframes, each 201 x 3)
gist <- "https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ericpgreen/5600c2455c1337def050/raw/123d11000e32d5c7be3d90e04f8fc67fb74e9e6e/miList.R"
source_url(gist)

# model
   mod <- ' total =~ v1 + v2 + v3 + v4 '

# cfa on 20 imputed data sets
  fit1 <- runMI(mod, data = miList, fun = "cfa")
  fitMeasures(fit1)
  # df=2, chisq=-4.95, tli=2.731, cfi=1

# cfa on 1 of the 20 imputed datasets
  fit2 <- cfa(mod, data=miList[[1]])
  fitMeasures(fit2)
  # df=2, chisq=1.069, tli=1.232, cfi=1

messages.author: cf1bcefdbd38a662
messages.subject: Re: interpreting fit measures from runMI on imputed data
parts:
Thanks for taking a look, Terry. You never want the response to be “wow” unless followed by “that is amazing!”.

MR and MPLUS return the same values. LMRR returns a positive chisq value.

fitMeasures(fit.mr)
# df=2, chisq=-4.950, tli=2.731, cfi=1

fitMeasures(fit.lmrr)
# df=2, chisq=0.559, tli=1.359, cfi=1

fitMeasures(fit.mplus)
# df=2, chisq=-4.950, tli=2.731, cfi=1
On January 26, 2016 at 5:55:27 AM, Terrence Jorgensen (tjorge...@gmail.com) wrote:

# cfa on 20 imputed data sets
  fit1 <- runMI(mod, data = miList, fun = "cfa")
  fitMeasures(fit1)
  # df=2, chisq=-4.95, tli=2.731, cfi=1

# cfa on 1 of the 20 imputed datasets
  fit2 <- cfa(mod, data=miList[[1]])
  fitMeasures(fit2)
  # df=2, chisq=1.069, tli=1.232, cfi=1

Wow, I've never seen a combined chi-squared come out negative before.  If you look at the formula for TLI, it's obvious that TLI will be quite large if you set chi-squared to a negative value.  So the weird results I'm sure all have to do with the combined chi-squared value.  I don't have the formulas in front of me, but the help page ?runMI has references you can check out.  I forget which one will be used by default, but you can try requesting each of the 3 methods and see if they all do the same thing:

fit.mr <- runMI(mod, data = miList, fun = "cfa", chi = "mr")
fit.lmrr <- runMI(mod, data = miList, fun = "cfa", chi = "lmrr")
fit.mplus <- runMI(mod, data = miList, fun = "cfa", chi = "mplus")

If Mauricio is reading this, he might have some insight since he wrote that source code.  But the combination rules for chi-squared are all pretty complex, so I'm not sure it would be obvious under what situations you could expect a negative combined value.  Perhaps when your model fits very well (so chi-sq < df) and there is little variability in chi-sq across imputations...

Terry

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: interpreting fit measures from runMI on imputed data
parts:
I have been called on this. Yes, it is right that the mr/mplus can return a negative chi-square. This is not too common, but mostly happens with simple models with very good fit, its simlar to when you find a TLI higher than 1, its not common but it can happend
The mr formula doesnt has anything that prevents it from being negative, while the lmrr does prevents the chi-square to be negative. 
If interested, we compare this conditions of negative chi-square to Mplus, and Mplus doesnt report the chi-square when this happens, and doesnt tells you that it was negative, it looks like some error happend but you dont know why. With MR\Mplus it can happend that the combine chi-squre can not be estimated, with runMI you can distinguish these conditions from a negative value, not in mplus.
LMRR is there as an alternative specially in conditions when MR cannot be computed

Still,in general common circunstances the MR is a better method to combine the ch-square (we still have to finish the paper talking about this). 
The other fit indices are estimates from the combine chi-square of the model and the combine chi-square of the null model. There are no good guidelines on how to combines the other fit indices, or if calculating them from the combine chi-squares are the best option. We follow this convention in runMI since it seems like the less risky method so far. We need more research about it.

Mauricio, 


Thanks for taking taking the time to comment. 


I’m still a bit confused because when I take the same approach on a completely different set of items for a different scale (this time 18 items loading onto 1 factor), I get the same pattern of values (e.g., cfi=1). Coincidence?


Expecting a poor fit, I even created a two-factor model with the first 6 of 18 items (3 on each factor) and got the same cfi=1 using a list of 20 imputed datasets. 


mod2 <- '

        tot1 =~ pss1 + pss2 + pss3

        '


fit2a<- runMI(mod2, data = miList, fun = "cfa", chi = "mr")

I should not see such a divergence, right? I don't think I'm the victim of a good fit, but I can't tell what might be going on. I'd be happy to post more data if anyone was curious enough to take a peek. 


Eric
